title: Staffing oscillation mitigation and scope anchoring playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Playbook that defines detection, mitigation, and governance for staffing oscillation during cycle execution and a paired scope-anchoring protocol. Goal: reduce mid-cycle role swaps and scope churn that cause downstream regressions in delivery and quality. Includes metrics, decision thresholds, temporary staffing policies (shadowing/pairing), crediting model for over-commit/decommit, and a lightweight runbook for PMs/eng leads to stabilize volatile lanes.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Draft created by Maya Patel. Rationale: recent cycles show >18% variance between planned and actual FTEs on critical lanes leading to repeated scope rework. Initial hypothesis: oscillation is driven by cross-team urgent bugs + unclear decommit signals.

2026-03-03 — Engineering feedback from Priya Singh: add instrumentation for 'commit drift' and suggest SLO guardrails to prevent swapping core reviewers mid-sprint. Priya attached telemetry doc: https://drive.redwood.internal/commit-drift-instrumentation-v1

2026-03-04 — Design note by Aaron Lee: scope-anchoring language should be non-prescriptive for feature teams but prescriptive for cross-team contracts. Proposed copy for template agreements added to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/scope-anchors

2026-03-05 — Decision log: adopt two-tier threshold model. If staffing oscillation rate (SOR) > 0.15 for 3 consecutive days -> enable temporary role shadowing; if SOR > 0.30 or customer-impacting work is blocked -> trigger emergency rebase meeting with GTM and Eng leads.

2026-03-06 — Action items assigned: Eng to add SOR dashboard tile (ENG-41211); PMs to trial scope-anchoring template on two actively shifting initiatives (PM-271828 and PM-842317); Ops to draft crediting ledger for decommits.

2026-03-08 — Interim note: Luca Romano ran tabletop with two leads; outcome: shadowing reduced handoff defects by estimated 22% in simulation, but increased short-term context-switch cost. Trade-off accepted for lanes flagged high-risk.

2026-03-09 — Review from Head of Product, Elena Rossi: approved playbook for pilot. Request: include explicit rollback window and clear owner for the crediting entries. Linking PRD and pilot plan: https://drive.redwood.internal/pm/pilots/staffing-oscillation-pilot-v1
2026-03-10 — Next steps: finalize runbook language, QA dashboards, schedule pilot kickoff 2026-03-16, and collect baseline metrics (SOR, commit-drift, scope-churn) for two-week pre-pilot comparison.
Artifacts: Confluence playbook draft (internal), Drive PRD, GitHub sample policy draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-playbooks/pulls/112
